video_title: Boogie, Chandler & Lou Get HEATED Over Wemby Being "Too Tired"!

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' resilience and collective effort against the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are a resilient team. They are never going to give up to the last buzzer.
quotes.quote: The Knicks are a resilient team. They are never going to give up to the last buzzer. They have been in this situation multiple times. Even when Brunson went down, Shamet comes in and gives them good minutes, Alvarado gives them good minutes. This was a collective effort. At a certain point of the game, Josh Hart scored three points, he might have been the most impactful player on the team in the game last night. He led the team in rebounds, assists, and steals while getting three points. Huge shout out to Josh Hart, he faced up Wembanyama like he wasn't even there in the corner. This team is just rolling, they are playing confident, they are tough.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's defensive impact and the Knicks' ability to finish
quotes.excerpt: I thought it was Wembanyama's impact that made it feel like they were playing better defense.
quotes.quote: I thought the Knicks did a great job of putting the Spurs' backs to the fire in that third quarter. They were up 14, Wembanyama goes out, and I said they are going to make a run when Wembanyama goes out because I thought it was Wembanyama's impact that made it feel like they were playing better defense than they were. New York was able to get into the paint whenever they wanted, but when they got to the paint, Wembanyama was there and they were kicking out, driving, kicking out. Once they subbed him out of the game, that is when you saw the lanes start opening up and New York started to be able to finish.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' dominant performance against Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Karl-Anthony Towns made it look easy going against Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: Karl-Anthony Towns made it look easy going against Wembanyama. Now there is going to be adjustments made, but I just love his attack mode, I love his aggression. I love the fact that he didn't settle, he kept trying to challenge Wembanyama and trying to put the ball on the floor and make him defend. I think they might have to make an adjustment, well, putting Wembanyama on someone else because I like Wembanyama floating, I like Wembanyama in the paint, and Karl-Anthony Towns is too good of a shooter to have him guarding him out in the perimeter.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of Karl-Anthony Towns' aggression in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: You just got to be aggressive. Forget what your role is, you just got to be a dog.
quotes.quote: It took some time to figure out and find that sweet spot that works for everybody. And it just also took Karl-Anthony Towns a chance, like, you just got to be aggressive. Forget what your role is, forget all of that, at the end of the day when you step inside the lines, you just got to be a dog. And I think Karl-Anthony Towns has found that in the postseason.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's heavy workload and impact on both ends
quotes.excerpt: You can't talk about how impactful he is on offense and defense every single play.
quotes.quote: You can't talk about how impactful he is on offense and defense every single play down the court and then not have anything for him when he gets tired. He gets tired, he is 22 years old, but he is involved in every single play down the floor on both ends of the court.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Tiredness is not an excuse for a star player
quotes.excerpt: Tired is not an excuse at that age.
quotes.quote: That is why they lost. He is 22, tired is not an excuse at that age.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The physical demands of being a star player
quotes.excerpt: Do we ever say LeBron James was tired?
quotes.quote: Do we ever say LeBron James was tired? Do we ever say these greats are tired? Now he is tired, that's the penalty of leadership.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The reality of Wembanyama's workload in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Last night we watched him play 17, 18 straight minutes, and somebody is going to get tired.
quotes.quote: The reality is last night we watched him play 17, 18 straight minutes, and somebody is going to get tired, especially if they are asking you to protect the rim, they ask you to protect the perimeter, they ask you to run the floor, they ask you to catch lobs, they ask you to screen and roll, they ask you to post up.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs' need for more production from their bench
quotes.excerpt: They got to get more production out of the bench.
quotes.quote: First of all, they got to get more production out of the bench. They have been getting outscored and outplayed from their bench in this series, in the first game and in the last series. They got to get more production out of the bench and that second group for him to be able to rest. Mitch Johnson did what he had to do to preserve this win. If you go up 14, 15 points, yes, I got to put Wembanyama back in the game so I can reserve my lead.
